newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks lower in choppy, cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks lower in choppy, cautious trade.

text.p: U.S. blue chips were slightly above session lows on Monday but shares were weak in choppy trade after Friday's steep losses and ahead of a stream of inflation-oriented economic data due later this week.

"The stock market is still worrying about what the bond market is doing," Henry Herrmann, chief investment officer, Waddell & Reed. "There's so much economic data coming out this week it will make it tough for much to happen in the market until we get through that."
A sharp rise in bond yields revived lurking rate and inflation fears on Friday, sending stocks lower.
On Monday, the bond market remained sluggish, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury off 2/32 at a 6.64 percent yield.

The Dow Jones Industrial average, which sank on Friday, was down three points at 8028 in mixed trade. The Nasdaq composite posted steeper declines, trading off about 10 points, or 0.57 percent, at 1589.

Herrmann said the stock market was also still digesting an earnings forecast from Coca-Cola Co, released last week, which raised concerns about high valuations afforded large-capitalization companies which usually post stable earnings growth.
